app.title: Make My Figure (Streamlit)
app.summary: A person loads a data table from an upload, a multi-sheet workbook or a bundled example. They can correct cells in place and optionally group the sample columns. They choose a plot type, either directly or from suggestions drawn from the table's profile, and map the table's columns to the plot's roles. They then adjust the typography, axes, legend and size, and can switch on a statistical test whose result is drawn on the figure. A preview with a readiness score updates as they work, and the finished figure is exported as SVG, PNG or PDF, together with a reproducible specification and a package that also holds a frozen copy of the data.

task.text: Turn a table of results into a figure ready for a manuscript, with its statistics drawn on, and save it in a form that can be reproduced.

data.text: A rectangular table of measurements, either one row per observation with group columns or a feature-by-sample matrix, with optional sample metadata.
data.item: a row of a results table: an observation, or a feature measured across samples

stage.text: making publication figures from analysed results, before writing up

mechanism.text: Numbered sidebar sections (data, plot type, style, column mapping, publication style, statistics) build a plot specification. The main pane re-renders the figure preview, a readiness score and the statistics table on every change, and export buttons at the bottom save the figure, its specification and a package with the frozen data.

field.text: publication figures and group-comparison statistics in the life sciences

workflow.name: configure a chart from a table and export it for publication

steps.here: Upload a CSV, TSV or XLSX file, pick a worksheet and its header row, or choose a bundled example for a plot type; a saved PlotSpec or Figure Package can be reopened instead.
An editable data grid shows the table with counts of rows, columns and numeric columns; cells can be edited and sample columns assigned to groups to make a grouped table.

steps.step: choose a chart and map columns to its roles
steps.here: Suggested figures with a match percentage, or a plot-type dropdown, then one dropdown per role (x, y, group, facet rows or columns) filled from the table's columns.

steps.step: style the figure to publication conventions
steps.here: Grouped expanders for figure width and dpi, typography, axes and labels, legend and colourbar; saved presets reapply these settings to new data.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Enable a statistical test (or auto-suggest), set the comparison mode, multiple-testing correction and what to do if assumptions fail; brackets or stars appear on the figure and a results table appears below.
The preview re-renders with a publication check and a 0–100 readiness score that lists issues and suggested fixes.
SVG, PNG or PDF download buttons, a PlotSpec JSON, and a Figure Package that bundles the spec, the frozen data and the stats records with checksums.

distinctive: the figure is described by a reproducible specification that can be reopened with its data to redraw it exactly
normality and equal-variance checks run before parametric tests, with an option to switch to the non-parametric alternative
a publication-readiness score lists layout issues before export
a single exportable package carries the frozen data, verified by checksums on reopen
multi-sheet workbooks are browsed sheet by sheet, and stale mappings are cleared when the sheet changes

parts.title: Data source
parts.summary: Loads the table from an upload, a worksheet of a workbook, a bundled example, a saved PlotSpec or a Figure Package.

parts.title: Table preview and grouping
parts.summary: Shows the loaded table as an editable grid with row and column counts, and lets sample columns be assigned to groups.

parts.title: Recommended figures
parts.summary: Profiles the table and suggests plot types with a match score and reason; clicking one loads it.

parts.title: Plot type and column mapping
parts.summary: Picks the plot type and maps table columns to each role the plot needs.

parts.title: Publication style and presets
parts.summary: Sets figure size, fonts, axes, legend and colourbar, and saves or applies presets of these settings.

parts.title: Statistics
parts.summary: Configures a statistical test drawn on the figure and shows its results table, method text and optional residual diagnostics.
